# Repeating Buttons

<!-- Generated by generate-swiftui-skill.py; edit the library sources. -->

Category: Feedback

Enable buttonRepeatBehavior so holding a button repeats its action. Clamp the value at its limits and give a small shake on rejected input; disable that motion when Reduce Motion is enabled. Inspired by PocketShelf (@PocketShelfApp).

- Before: Repeated taps; silent boundary
- After: Hold to repeat; boundary feedback

APIs: `buttonRepeatBehavior`, `keyframeAnimator`, `accessibilityReduceMotion`

## Complete improved example

Adapt the behavior to the app; demonstration controls and values are illustrative.

```swift
import SwiftUI

struct RepeatingButtonsDoExample: View {
    @State private var page = 1
    @State private var boundaryHits = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        // excerpt:start
        VStack {
            Text("Page \(page) of 5")
                .monospacedDigit()
            HStack {
                Button("Previous", systemImage: "minus") { changePage(by: -1) }
                Button("Next", systemImage: "plus") { changePage(by: 1) }
            }
            .labelStyle(.iconOnly)
            .buttonRepeatBehavior(.enabled)
            .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: CGFloat.zero, trigger: boundaryHits) { content, offset in
                content.offset(x: reduceMotion ? 0 : offset)
            } keyframes: { _ in
                LinearKeyframe(-4, duration: 0.06)
                LinearKeyframe(4, duration: 0.06)
                LinearKeyframe(0, duration: 0.06)
            }
            Text("Hold a button to try it").font(.caption)
        }
        // excerpt:end
    }

    private func changePage(by delta: Int) {
        let next = min(5, max(1, page + delta))
        if next == page {
            if !reduceMotion { boundaryHits += 1 }
        }
        page = next
    }
}
```
